title: 1-04 Barren Sea
body:
### Background and Hook(s)

- This is likely the third area explored by the players, and is tailored toward the level bands of 7 - 11 and 9 - 13, meaning creatures with CR maxing out at about 13.
- The waters of the Barren Sea have almost ten times the salt content of the other seas of Eberron. Few plants or animals can survive in these waters. A side effect of this is that the waters of the Barren Sea are surprisingly buoyant; anyone swimming in the Barren Sea has advantage on checks made to stay afloat. Some sages theorize that the Barren Sea’s effect is somehow created and sustained by a supernatural force—for while hypersa linity is typically a natural phenomenon, these waters defy all attempts to explain them.
- Much to the bewilderment of scholars and sailors alike, a massive nondetection effect blankets the barren waters and anything on them—and its effects begin and end almost precisely where the hypersalinity does. Mystical navigation tools become unreliable in barren waters, and navigators must be prepared to use mundane techniques.
- The Barren Sea isn’t a resource to be harvested; it’s a deadly obstacle to be crossed, an aquatic desert.

### Characters and Locations

- 

#### ★5: Pale Fall (Dolurrh MZ)
 - [ ]  
>The water turns grey and hazed ahead, as if a blizzard drifts beneath the waves. Countless pale flecks fall in slow motion all around you — ash, silt, fragments of something once alive — muffling sound and swallowing distance. Shapes loom and fade within the pale fall: long ribs arching like broken hulls, a skull wider than a ship’s beam, a tangle of tentacles suspended in stillness. Nothing moves quickly here. Even your own wake seems reluctant to follow.

- The entire region is saturated with thick **marine snow**, reducing visibility and dampening sound; distant shapes resolve only at close range, creating constant uncertainty and slow, oppressive exploration.
- Suspended in the upper water column are drifting skeletons and partially preserved corpses, caught in a slow downward fall that never seems to complete. Among them: a massive aboleth skeleton with its ribcage intact, twisted tentacular remains of unknown leviathans, and several dead Deep One cultists still clutching ritual objects.
- No strong currents exist; movement feels laborious, and creatures that stop swimming drift downward at a sluggish, inevitable pace.
- **The Memory Anchor**. Embedded within the ribcage of the aboleth skeleton is a faintly glowing organ-like mass of preserved neural tissue, partially crystallized by planar influence. Approaching within close range triggers intrusive sensory flashes — alien cities, psychic domination, and the sensation of drowning in someone else’s thoughts. These visions should allude to the living aboleth, the Aboleth Temple, and any nearby unvisited sahuagin kar'lassa cities.
- Roll on the [[C06 The City Between#Random Discovery|Random Discovery]] table to determine what's found here.

>[!danger]- **Suffocating Stillness (Environmental Lair Action)**
In the densest parts of the Pale Fall, creatures that Dash or take strenuous actions must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution save or gain one level of ennui. See Ennui in [[Aryth (Dolurrh)#Universal Properties]].

#### ★5: Hal'dol
 - [ ]  
>Light fades quickly, swallowed by drifting silt and towering skeletal remains. Massive bones form arches and walls, lashed together with black coral and sinew. Sound feels distant and muffled, as though the water itself is exhausted. Pale motes drift slowly, brushing against you like cold breath.

- The smallest of the great cities, Hal’dol is a center for necromantic research. The skulls of great leaders and priests from across the Dominion are preserved in the Bone Library, where sahuagin mediums can use speak with dead to consult with them.
- **Activity**. Public reanimation rites, where citizens decide whether the fallen earn rest or continued service.

##### Locations
- **Ossuary Vats**. Where corpses are rendered into obedient undead labor or soldiers.
- **Echo Pools**. Where lingering impressions of the dead are drawn out for intelligence.
- **Spawning Pools**. Few eggs are laid here. Fewer still hatch. And those that do are... wrong... neither truly dead nor truly alive, but operating somewhere in-between. This makes them especially terrifying, as they are difficult to harm and especially do not retreat.

##### Characters
- **Dolmera the Still** (NE female sahuagin necromancer). Claims she has already given her soul to Dolurrh and speaks with unsettling calm.

#### ★5: Underwater Graveyard
 - [ ]  
>The seabed stretches in every direction as a flat expanse of dark silt marked by orderly rows of bones. Massive ribcages rise in parallel lines like the ruins of vaulted ceilings, their spines aligned as if deliberately placed. Skulls—some the size of houses—rest half-sunken but intact, eye sockets open and unbroken. Smaller skeletons cluster in arcs and circles, including humanoid forms still arranged as if kneeling. Nothing disturbs the arrangement; even the sediment between the bones lies smooth and undisturbed.

- This abyssal plain sits far below Hal’dol; Dolurrh’s influence remains only as preservation and emotional dulling. The dead do not animate easily, but neither do they decay.
- The graveyard contains leviathans, sahuagin war-beasts, unknown tentacled colossi, shipwrecks, and the unmistakable skeletal dome and rib structure of an aboleth embedded in the sediment.
- Many remains appear intentionally oriented—long skeletons parallel to one another, cultists grouped in ritual patterns, wrecks aligned in the same direction—as though currents or unseen forces sorted them into burial rows.
- Hooked onto one of the skeletons, noticeable with a DC 14 Perception check, is a **Ring of Mind Shielding**.
- One leviathan rib bears etched Aquan script: “Belief gives it form.” The script style matches kuo-toa ruins in the Dark Sea.
- The Deep One cultists are arranged in perfect arcs facing the aboleth skull, not randomly scattered. Their hands clutch spiral-carved shells identical to symbols seen near the murder site in Tidecrown.
- When the PCs arrive, undead creatures begin to emerge from the graveyard and continue to emerge in waves every few rounds. Any thunder damage, heavy impact, or reckless movement triggers an immediate new wave of creatures.

`encounter: 1d4+1: Ghast`
`encounter: 1d6+1: Sharkjaw Skeleton`
`encounter: 1: Wraith`

#### ★6: Great Reef (Thelanis MZ)
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-05-04
>The reef rises in vast terraces of impossible color, coral branches curving into arches and spirals as though shaped by deliberate hands. Glow squid drift in slow constellations above, their lights pulsing in coordinated patterns instead of scattering at your approach. Electric eels coil lazily in open trenches, arcs of lightning traveling between mineral nodes without striking. Large reef creatures pass close and unafraid, circling with open curiosity rather than threat.

- The reef functions like a courtly space rather than an ecosystem: creatures are unusually calm and responsive, and no native fauna initiates violence.
- Coral formations subtly resemble thrones, crowns, arches, and amphitheaters, reinforcing narrative symbolism over natural randomness.
- Glow squid gather in spirals overhead when significant conversation occurs, their light patterns forming recognizable shapes—most notably a crowned, tentacled silhouette.
- At the center of a natural coral amphitheater stands **Lady Thalessine of the Gilded Current** (CG female sea elf fey courtier), who does not demand tribute or combat, only conversation.
- **The Parable**. Thalessine gestures upward as the glow squid tighten into a luminous spiral and speaks. After delivering the parable, which alludes to the creation of the overlord from the thoughts and beliefs of the kuo-toa, any of her responses remain cryptic.
>“A priest once found a word with no meaning.
But it shone like a black pearl when spoken.
He taught it to his followers.
They sang it in chorus.
They wept when they spoke it.
They swore it meant everything.
And one day… something answered to it.”

The squid briefly form the silhouette of a crowned, tentacled figure before dissolving. She asks:
>“Did the name find its owner… or did the owner find its name?”

#### ★6: Hal'thela
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-05-11 (unfinished)
- Hal'thela is not built around a kar'lassa — it is built inside one. The sahuagin of this region have inhabited the gut of a living leviathan for generations, carving permanent chambers into calcified organ tissue and cultivating bioluminescent parasites for light. The creature is ancient, enormous, and indifferent to the civilization inside it.
- The party enters through the maw when the kar'lassa surfaces to feed. The dungeon progresses downward through three levels — Throat, Viscera, Deep Organs — and ends at the Core Infection, where a massive parasitic organism has taken root in the kar'lassa's central nerve cluster, slowly killing it. A sahuagin elder named Vrethis the Consumed has been attempting to purge it for years and is running out of time.
- When the final parasite is destroyed, the kar'lassa convulses and expels the party through its mouth in a violent surge of water.
- Three hardened **nerve ganglia** (biological keys) are embedded in major parasitic hosts: one in Level 1, two in Level 2. These ganglia unlock an optional sealed organ vault in Level 3. Level 2 ends with the vertical drop adapted from TotNG Area 18. Level 3 contains the lungs, a surviving sahuagin NPC, the optional vault, and the final parasite chamber.

##### General Features
- **Surfaces**. Every wall, floor, and ceiling is living tissue — warm, faintly slick, and subtly pulsing. Handholds exist but shift when weight is applied. Footing is never certain.
- **Light**. Bioluminescent clusters of symbiotic organisms cling to walls throughout, casting dim blue-green light in every room. Darkness spells extinguish them temporarily; they resume within 1 minute.
- **Contractions**. Loud thunder damage, explosions, or heavy impacts trigger involuntary muscular contractions. Each creature in the current room must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet in a direction determined by the room's current flow (typically downward or toward center).
- **Current**. Water movement trends consistently downward until Level 3's finale. Swimming with the current costs no additional movement; against it costs double.

##### Level 1 — The Throat

###### H1. The Maw
_(TotNG Area 1 — Entrance with Gargoyle Overwatch)_
> Enamel ridges the size of longships frame the opening like a cathedral arch. The teeth are ancient ivory, worn flat by millennia of feeding, but the gum tissue between them is raw and faintly pink. The jaw opens and closes in slow, glacial rhythm. Water surges inward with each opening, then stills. The space smells of salt, crushed shell, and something animal that has no name.

- The Maw is 80 feet wide and 60 feet from floor to palate. Calcified ridges of plaque between the teeth provide cover and handholds, and serve as nesting platforms for the Grells that ambush from above.
- **Encounter.** A Grell clings to the upper ridges, using its tentacles to brace against the tooth surface. It drops when the party passes the midpoint of the chamber, attempting to grapple and paralyze separated targets. If the party has a light source, the Grell has already noticed them and will not be surprised.
- **Treasure.** Lodged in a crevice between two molars is a salt-crusted satchel from a previous victim: 60 gp in assorted coin, a [[Potion of Water Breathing]], and a waterlogged journal written in Aquan. The journal belongs to a locathah cartographer who mapped the kar'lassa's internal geography before dying here. His maps are accurate for Rooms H1–H7; H8 onward is blank with a final entry: _"The beating is wrong. Don't go deeper."_

`encounter: 1: Grell`

###### H2. Intake Channel
_(TotNG Level 1 Underground River feature)_
> The current takes hold immediately — not violent, but insistent. The channel is perhaps fifteen feet across, its walls rippling with slow peristaltic motion like the throat of something swallowing. Alcoves punch into the tissue at irregular intervals, deep enough to brace against. The floor is slick, the ceiling low, and the water moves with a purpose that has nothing to do with you.

- The channel runs 120 feet with a consistent 10-foot drop in elevation. It functions as difficult terrain for creatures moving against the current; creatures moving with it gain 10 feet of additional movement per turn.
- Three alcoves allow temporary shelter. Resting in an alcove for a full round stops forced movement for that round.
- The channel forks 80 feet in — the left fork is a dead-end bile duct (DC 13 Perception to notice before committing) that deposits characters in a shallow acid pool dealing `dice:2d6` acid damage per round. The right fork leads to H3.

###### H3. Regenerative Sac
_(TotNG Area 9 — Magic Fountain)_
> The channel widens into a domed cavity where the walls pulse visibly, squeezing rhythmically around a central organ the size of a wagon. The organ is translucent; fluid inside it glows amber, shifting with each contraction to pale gold. The fluid has saturated the floor to ankle depth. Everything here smells faintly sweet, like overripe fruit, and the light from the organ throws no shadows.

- The organ is a regenerative sac — a biological reservoir of restorative fluid. A creature that drinks directly from the sac or submerges their head rolls on the following table (d6): 
	- 1–2: regain 2d8 hit points; 
	- 3-4: gain advantage on Constitution and death saves for 1 hour; 
	- 5: temporary bioluminescence — shed dim light in a 10-foot radius for 1 hour; 
	- 6: nothing, but the taste is extraordinary.
- A Chuul has nested in the sac's underside, anchored by its tendrils to the organ wall. It feeds off the regenerative fluid and has grown significantly larger than typical. It attacks when any creature touches the organ.
- **Nerve Ganglion #1** is embedded in the Chuul's thoracic cavity, visible as a faint glow through its carapace. Retrieving it requires either killing the Chuul or a DC 16 Sleight of Hand check while it is grappled or incapacitated. Once detached, the ganglion's outer membrane seals over into a smooth, dry, palm-sized ovoid that pulses and tugs toward sealed membrane sockets within 10 feet — its purpose is self-evident.

`encounter: 1: Chuul`

###### H4. Parasite Lure Sac
_(TotNG Area 12 — Trapped Chest)_
> A translucent cyst the size of a carriage hangs from the ceiling on thick organic stalks, swaying gently in the current. Something moves inside it — a slow, rotating mass of smaller shapes. The light through its membrane casts rippling shadows across the floor. The cyst is leaking, and the fluid pooling below it smells of deep water and copper.

- The cyst is a parasitic trap — an organism that mimics biological treasure to lure hosts. It contains 1d6 smaller parasites (reskin as Intellect Devourers; they are not psychic, just ravenous) suspended in nutrient fluid.
- If a creature approaches within 5 feet without first cutting the stalks (DC 14 Perception to identify the trap mechanism), the cyst ruptures and engulfs them. An engulfed creature is restrained, begins suffocating, and takes 1d6 piercing damage per round. Cutting through the cyst wall from outside requires 15 slashing damage (AC 10); from inside requires 10 slashing damage.
- **Treasure.** A previous victim is suspended at the center of the cyst, fully preserved. The body is a sahuagin warrior wearing a _+1 Trident_ and a `wonder:Necklace of Adaptation` — the necklace kept them alive long enough to be preserved before it ran out.

`encounter: 1d6: Intellect Devourer`

###### H5. Esophageal Plunge
_(TotNG Area 17 — Underground Waterfall)_
> The channel ends at a vertical shaft — an organic funnel where the walls press inward in overlapping folds of muscle. The current accelerates sharply at the lip, and looking down reveals only darkness and the distant sound of fluid movement. The walls on the way down are studded with hooked barbs of calcified tissue, spaced irregularly, as though once meant to slow something.

- The plunge drops 40 feet into Level 2's basin (H6). The current pushes creatures over the edge on their turn unless they brace against the wall (DC 13 Athletics). Braced creatures can attempt to climb down (Athletics DC 14, disadvantage due to the current) or simply drop.
- A Grell clings to the mid-shaft wall, disguised as a fold of membrane. It drops onto a falling creature that fails a DC 15 Perception check, grappling mid-fall. A grappled creature falls with the Cloaker attached and lands prone in H6.
- The barbs deal `dice:1d4` piercing damage to any creature that falls rather than climbs.

`encounter: 1: Grell`

##### Level 2 — The Viscera

###### H6. Digestive Basin
_(TotNG Area 64 — Base of the Waterfall)_
> You land in a broad, low-ceilinged cavity where the floor is not floor but fluid. The liquid is thick and faintly acidic, clouded the color of old amber. Visibility beyond 20 feet is near-zero. The sound of digestion is constant here: rhythmic gurgling, the shift of fluid pressure, and a deeper percussive thud coming from somewhere below. Something large stirs in the murk ahead.

- The basin is 60 feet across and filled with enzymatic fluid to a depth of 6 feet. Movement through the fluid costs double. Prolonged contact (more than 3 consecutive rounds submerged) deals 1d4 acid damage per round.
- Visibility is heavily obscured beyond 20 feet.
- An Otyugh has been living in the basin for years, feeding on organic waste. It is territorial but not immediately hostile — it will display (rearing, thrashing tentacles) before attacking. A successful DC 14 Animal Handling check convinces it the party is not prey; it cannot be reasoned with beyond that.
- **Nerve Ganglion #2** is encased in a calcified nodule on the Otyugh's back. It is not visible without a DC 14 Perception check. Removing it requires killing the Otyugh or 10 minutes of careful extraction with a blade while it is restrained or willing. Once detached, it behaves as described in H3.
- The basin drains toward two exits: a membrane valve leading to H7 and a low crawlway leading to H8 (only directly visible with a DC 18 Investigation check).

`encounter: 1: Otyugh`

###### H7. Peristaltic Loop
_(TotNG Area 19 — Gravity Ring)_
> The passage is circular — not roughly, but perfectly, as though bored out by a machine. The walls contract in waves, rhythmic and slow, each pulse traveling from one end of the tunnel to the other in a visible ripple. Moving against the direction of the pulse is like walking into a slow-moving wall that never quite stops pushing.

- The loop is 60 feet long and curves back on itself, depositing characters slightly deeper in Level 2. Contractions move in 6-second intervals. Moving with the contraction costs normal movement. Moving against requires two Strength checks: DC 12 followed by DC 16. Failure on the second check reverses the character's position by 20 feet.
- Three Flumphs cling to the ceiling at the curve of the loop. They are non-hostile symbiotic scavengers. A creature with telepathy or Detect Thoughts who makes contact receives a wordless impression: something ahead is _wrong_ — the sensation of a heartbeat that skips.

###### H8. Spore Sac
_(TotNG Area 63 — Gas-Filled Room)_
> You're deposited into a chamber where the air is thick with metabolic vapor — grey-white clouds drifting in slow eddies, clinging to armor and hair. The walls are studded with dark, puckered ducts, each sealed with a membrane that pulses independently. The largest duct, nearly four feet across, has already ruptured; the membrane hangs in shreds, and something wet and glistening moves in the dark behind it.

- The chamber is filled with toxic metabolic vapor. At initiative count 20, each creature must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned until the start of their next turn; poisoned creatures take 1d6 poison damage at the same time.
- The ruptured duct has released two Gibbering Mouthers fused to the wall tissue. They cannot move from their position but their attack range is 20 feet and their gibbering affects the full room.
- Three intact ducts remain. A creature can use an action to seal a duct (DC 13 Medicine check or improvised materials). Sealing all three reduces the vapor DC to 9.
- **Nerve Ganglion #3** is embedded in a calcified growth on the largest duct. Retrieving it requires defeating or bypassing the Gibbering Mouthers, as they attack anything moving toward the duct wall. Once detached, it behaves as described in H3.
- **Treasure.** Three sahuagin corpses are fused to the wall tissue — a patrol caught when the duct ruptured. Combined, they carry 120 gp in trade goods, a `wonder:Brooch of Shielding`, and a sealed cylinder containing a message in Sahuagin addressed to Vrethis. The message describes the infection's spread and requests evacuation orders. It was never delivered.

`encounter: 2: Gibbering Mouther`

###### H9. Immune Response Shaft
_(TotNG Area 18 — Devil Pit)_
> The shaft drops into darkness. The walls are dense, fibrous, and almost black — a stark contrast to the warmer tissue elsewhere. Thin filaments extend from the walls into open air like hairs raised against static electricity. They tremble as you approach.

- The shaft is 30 feet deep. Disturbing the filament tissue triggers parasite swarms — one swarm per 5 feet of disturbed wall, maximum 4 active at once. A creature that controls their descent to the center of the shaft by whatever means — rope, _Feather Fall_, a spread cloak, a clean jump — avoids triggering the swarms entirely. A creature that falls and sticks the landing in the center (DC 12 Acrobatics) also avoids them, but takes normal falling damage.
- Climbing the walls without a rope is not viable; the tissue grips and the filaments trigger on contact.

`encounter: 1: Swarm of Insects`

##### Level 3 — Deep Organs

###### H10. Lungs of the Leviathan
_(TotNG Area 37 — Winds of Pandemonium)_
> The shaft opens into a vast cavity — the largest space yet encountered. It is not a room; it is an organ. Membrane platforms of translucent tissue float at varying heights, connected by thick fibrous cords that stretch and contract slowly. The ceiling disappears into darkness. Two enormous lobes of lung tissue fill the far walls, inflating and deflating in long, slow cycles. The air here is dry, thin, and tastes of salt and ozone. And then the inhalation begins.

- The chamber is 120 feet wide and 80 feet tall, with membrane platforms at 10-foot, 30-foot, and 50-foot elevations connected by fibrous cords (Athletics DC 11 to climb). Falling from a platform deals normal falling damage.
- Every 3 rounds, the lung chamber cycles — **Inhalation** (DC 14 Strength save or be pulled 20 feet toward the far wall), then **Exhalation** (DC 14 Strength save or be pushed 20 feet toward the center shaft).
- An inflamed nerve cluster is visible as a red-orange mass on the left lung wall, accessible from the 30-foot platform. Striking it with any fire, lightning, or piercing damage above 10 in a single hit triggers an immediate violent cycle: all creatures suffer both Inhalation and Exhalation effects in the same round.

###### H11. The Survivor
> A narrow recess in the capillary tissue, barely wide enough for two people to sit side by side. The sahuagin inside is scarred across most of her visible skin, her fin crests burned flat by acid exposure. She does not reach for a weapon. She holds up one hand, palm out, and says something in Sahuagin. Then, after a pause, she says it again in halting Aquan: _"Don't. Touch. The walls."_

- **Vrethis the Consumed** (NE female sahuagin, veteran) is the elder responsible for Hal'thela's maintenance. She was leading a purge team into the core infection when the immune response shaft sealed behind them. Her team is dead. She has survived 11 days in this recess on tissue and condensed moisture.
- Vrethis is not friendly, but she is pragmatic. She will share everything she knows — contraction rhythms, the ganglion vault mechanism, the nature of the core infection — in exchange for a sworn commitment to get her out alive. She does not believe they will succeed. She will help anyway.
- She knows: the final chamber holds a Behir that arrived as a juvenile parasite decades ago and has since merged with the nerve cluster; the ganglion vault contains something placed there by the city's founders; the kar'lassa has perhaps two weeks before the infection kills it.
- If shown the sealed message from H8, she reads it, folds it, and pockets it. She does not comment.

###### H12. Ganglion Vault (Optional)
> Three recesses flank the sealed membrane, each rimmed with a dark socket of organic tissue. The membrane itself is pale and thick — not calcified but structured, deliberate. It does not look grown. It looks placed.

- Inserting all three ganglia simultaneously (requires three creatures acting in the same turn, or one creature with three actions) causes the membrane to retract cleanly. No alarm, no resistance.
- **Treasure.** A `wonder:Staff of Thunder and Lightning`, wrapped in sharkskin bindings, a `wonder:Ring of Free Action`, and a carved stone tablet in archaic Sahuagin confirming that the vault was sealed by the city's founders as a gift to whoever could reach it — anyone who made it this far had already demonstrated they could survive the kar'lassa.
- Vrethis, if present, reads the tablet and is visibly shaken. She says nothing.

###### H13. Core Infection
> The final chamber is a cathedral of failing tissue. The walls are dark and slick with necrotic fluid. At the center, coiled around a pulsing nerve cluster the size of a house, is the Behir — but calling it that understates what it has become. Its scales have fused with the organ tissue; its forelimbs have merged into the wall. Its eyes open when you enter. It does not move. It watches. Then the chamber contracts, and it decides.

- The **Behir** (CR 11) has partially merged with the nerve cluster and cannot move more than 30 feet from its position. It uses the chamber as lair actions.
- **Lair Actions (initiative count 20):**
    - **Muscular Surge.** The floor heaves. Each creature must succeed on DC 14 Dexterity save or fall prone.
    - **Fluid Expulsion.** A jet of enzymatic fluid erupts toward one creature. Ranged attack (+6), 3d6 acid damage.
    - **Neural Spasm.** The nerve cluster pulses. One creature the Behir can see must succeed on DC 14 Wisdom save or use its reaction to move 10 feet toward the Behir.
- **On death,** the chamber convulses. All creatures must succeed on DC 15 Strength save or take 2d8 bludgeoning damage and fall prone. The internal current reverses, propelling the party upward through the dungeon and depositing them in H5/H6. The kar'lassa's mouth opens; they are expelled into open water.
- **Treasure.** Fused within the Behir's merged tissue, accessible after 10 minutes of extraction, is an _Iridescent Carapace Plate_ (reskin of _Armor of Resistance: Lightning_) — a suit of plate armor grown from the kar'lassa's calcified hide over the Behir's decades of growth. It fits a Medium creature.

`encounter: 1: Behir`

#### ✣10: Dar Jin (Port)
 - [x]  
- Dar Jin is a major city and the largest port of Corvagura. The city is a major trade hub, as it is the most well-known place for traders from Xen'drik and Khorvaire to acquire Sarlonan goods or gain permission to enter into Corvagura.
- Dar Jin is the most industrial city on the coast, and is said to be where Tidecrown was built, shortly after the Second Sundering. The city is still considered local by the inhabitants, who have free right of travel to it.
- The *Crosscurrent* is found docked here. They may answer questions, relay Secrets and Clues, or point the party toward an important location.

#### ✣11: Dvaarnava and Ardhmen (Ports)
 - [x]  
- Dvaarnava is located on the southernmost tip of Adar. While most of Adar's coastline is sheer cliffs, ships can dock at Dvaarnava by traveling past a maze of stone spires into a natural cavern in the cliffs. Most of the population of Dvaarnava live in grottoes farther up the cliffs to be safe from the stormy waters. As Adar's only port, most of the region's trade flows through the port. Most trade is done with Ardhmen in Syrkarn, but some ships travel further to Khorvaire.
- Ardhmen is a story port city, and the closest location to the Aventi's former home of the Aventus islands. Some descendants of the ancient Aventi still live here, but are no longer anything like their ancestors (rednecks).
- The *Crosscurrent* is found docked here. They may answer questions, relay Secrets and Clues, or point the party toward an important location.

#### ✣11: Aventi Ruins
 - [ ]  
- A drowned pre-Inspired city on the seafloor off the Aventus Islands. The sentira bowl being pursued by The Pilgrim sits in a collapsed communal dreaming hall at the deepest intact level.
- **Sea spawn and deep scions** fill the upper ruins — former Aventi explorers transformed by prolonged exposure to the bowl's psychic bleed. A **brain coral** colony has grown around the bowl itself and defends it if removal is attempted.
- **The bowl:** Handling it without preparation triggers a DC 15 Wisdom save — failure delivers the kuo-toa severance vision and `dice:2d8` psychic damage (half on a success).

`encounter: 2: Sea Spawn, 2: Deep Scion`
`encounter: 1: Brain Coral`

#### ⚔2: Barren Sea
 - [x]  ✅ 2026-05-04
- Positioned between the continents of Argonnesson and Sarlona, draconic and psionic-empowered creatures are common sites here.

|  d6 | Encounter                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --: | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|   1 | **Dead Float Expanse**. The sea is glass-flat and unnaturally buoyant, crusted with drifting salt sheets that knock softly against the hull. No current, no life, no wake. Swimming is effortless but disorienting; sudden movement or diving kicks up blinding clouds of salt crystals that foul vision and instruments.                                                                                                                                         |
|   2 | **Risia Cold Front**. The water temperature drops in moments, frosting exposed surfaces and flash-freezing spray into brittle ice. Rigging stiffens, hull seams creak, and crew suffer numbing cold shock. Lingering risks structural damage or crew exhaustion as Risia’s influence presses outward.                                                                                                                                                             |
|   3 | **Drowned Maiden (CR ~10)**. A preserved wreck hangs suspended in hypersaline water, its timbers bleached white and intact like a fossil. The Drowned Maiden drifts through the ruin, replaying the final moments of the crew, while two Shellycoats lurk amid the salt-encrusted debris. Hostility triggers if the wreck is boarded, looted, or magically disturbed.<br>`encounter: 1: Drowned Maiden, 2: Shellycoat`                                            |
|   4 | **Shimmer Seals (CR 10)**. Two seal-shaped forms glide through the water, bodies composed of refracted ice-light and drifting frost motes. They are not animals but planar constructs born of overlapping Risia influence. Heat, spellcasting, or aggressive maneuvering provokes them into ramming passes that flash-freeze targets.<br>`encounter: 2: Shimmer Seal`                                                                                             |
|   5 | **Demonglass Needle-Teeth**. Jagged spires of black demonglass thrust up from the seabed like rows of serrated fangs. The water is perfectly still, offering no warning or drift—any misjudged movement risks collision with edges sharp enough to slice hull plating, armor, and flesh alike. Maneuvering through the field requires slow, deliberate navigation; combat here is especially dangerous, as forced movement or loss of control can be fatal.       |
|   6 | **Lorelei of the Salt Silence (CR ~11)**. A thin, hollow song echoes through the water as a Lorelei drifts amid a field of perfectly still, hypersaline water. Her voice feeds on _memory_, not desire, drawing creatures into a dead zone where thoughts blur and reactions slow. Three Nihilethic Zombies, preserved by salt rather than decay, drift nearby as passive echoes until the song is resisted or disrupted.  <br>`encounter: 1 Lorelei, 3 Deep One` |

#### ⚔3: Sea of Lost Souls
 - [ ]  
- With its proximity to the manifest zone to Dolurrh, and the sad memories of Xen'drik's history, the Sea of Lost Souls is awash with spirits, undead, and other seemingly unnatural phenomenon.

#### ⚔3: Giant Ruins
 - [ ]  
> The ruins emerge from the silt in broken enormity—archways that once framed doorways now frame nothing, stone tablets etched with script too large to read at normal scale, and collapsed walls that form new terrain across the seabed. Everything is intact enough to suggest grandeur and ruined enough to confirm it is gone. At the center of the wreckage, a figure sits cross-legged among the debris, still as the stone around her, a greatspear resting across her knees. She is watching you already.

- The ruins are the remnants of a storm giant outpost from the Age of Giants—not a city, but a waystation and vault complex. The scale of the architecture is disorienting; doorways are 40 feet tall, stairs are sized for creatures three times the height of a human, and the collapsed sections create a maze of enormous debris.
- The ruins are not dangerous by themselves, but the scale creates natural chokepoints, vertical terrain, and poor sightlines that make any combat here uniquely threatening.
- **Varreth the Unfinished** has sat at the center of these ruins for longer than most civilizations have existed. She does not know precisely what she guards. She knows only that she was told to guard it, that the one who told her is long dead, and that she has not yet been relieved of duty. She is not delusional — she understands the civilization is gone — but she has decided that the absence of orders to stand down is itself an order to remain.
- Varreth will speak to the players openly and without hostility. She is curious about the outside world in the detached way of someone who stopped expecting it to surprise her. She will answer questions about the ruins, the giants, and the vault freely. She will not allow entry to the vault under any circumstances, and she will not be persuaded otherwise by argument alone.
- **The Vault**. The vault is sealed beneath the ruins, accessible through a single enormous stone door engraved with storm giant script. A DC 16 History check identifies the script as a warding inscription. The door is not magically sealed; Varreth is the seal.
	- Inside the vault, suspended in a current of perpetually circulating water, is a **Prismatic Pearl** (any the players haven't discovered yet, or random).
- **Getting Past Varreth** There are two paths:
	- **Defeat her in combat.** Varreth will not yield. She has no reason to survive the loss of her post, and she knows it. She fights to the death.
	- **Demonstrate worthiness.** Varreth's original orders, recoverable from tablet fragments scattered through the ruins (three DC 14 Investigation checks, requires reading Giant), instruct her to surrender the vault's contents to one proven worthy of bearing it. A player who speaks Giant may also simply ask her what her orders are — she will tell them plainly, having waited centuries for someone to ask. What constitutes worthiness is her judgment to make, but she is not arbitrary: she is looking for someone with a clear purpose, the capability to act on it, and an honest account of what they intend. The full truth about the Deep One, the pearls, and what is at stake satisfies her on all three counts.

`encounter: 1: Storm Giant`

##### Characters

- **Varreth the Unfinished** (LN female storm giant, self-appointed warden). Enormous even by giant standards, with skin the grey-blue of deep water and hair matted into thick cords by centuries of salt. Her armor is long since fused to her skin in places, and she has stopped trying to remove it. She speaks slowly and precisely, as though conserving words she has been rationing for a very long time. She is not sad, not angry, and not afraid—she is simply _waiting_, with the patience of something that has forgotten what it was waiting for.
